quotes.text: Today’s AI is already outdated, and that’s how fast this is moving, and I think we’re right to take a look at this ahead of the 2024 election,

The AI Taskforce has wrapped up! We heard from experts in healthcare, law enforcement and education on how AI improves efficiency, but we also recognized the challenges. It’s all about balancing innovation with responsibility. Excited for what’s next!

Regulating AI in our state.
 
During last week's AI Taskforce meeting, we discussed the benefits and potential pitfalls of AI in our state; specifically in K-12 education, higher education and our workforce. (1/4) https://t.co/B6zm1T9WQk

Today we discussed: 
1. Impact of AI on the workforce and manufacturing 
2. AI's impact on copyrighting 
3. Establishing AI laws for the private sector 
4. Civilian cybersecurity

These are critical topics, and I am grateful to be a part of these proactive conversations… (2/3)

The AI Task Force met for the second time today. 

Our task force continued to explore the emerging industry of AI and discuss where future regulation could be needed to keep up with rapidly changing technology. (1/3) https://t.co/phGTj6AGJB

For two years in a row, I introduced legislation to require data centers, before construction, to disclose to the community their expected utility and water usage and provide a site assessment to determine the possible effects on the community of the construction and operation. [...] In Congress, I will always fight for full transparency on data centers. I will never let decisions that affect a community be made without that community's voice.

Congresswoman Victoria Spartz helped make Indiana one of the most data-friendly states in the country – full stop. She took campaign donations from big tech companies like Amazon and utility companies like Duke Energy, then voted for a version of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act that would have removed state and local governments’ ability to create guardrails against AI data center expansions that harm Hoosiers and harm communities

Congresswoman Spartz is not serious about this issue, because if she were, she would introduce the same legislation that I did in the Indiana Senate in Congress: putting communities in control of whether and when data centers are built, and ensuring no costs are passed on to ratepayers
AI does good things but can also be used for nefarious reasons and we want to make sure we put some guardrails around that,
Victoria Spartz accusing our campaign of using AI imagery in our ad is another desperate attempt to distract voters from her corruption. https://t.co/FwgRJ31mYj
Look, these data centers, they’re eating up our electricity. There’s no reason to look elsewhere, why we have high utility rates in our state.
